reason: The text contains multiple named individual characters who are clearly regular people (humans): Moses (מֹשֶׁה), Joshua (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ), Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), and Hur (חוּר). These named figures are described performing ordinary human actions—commanding troops, holding up arms, sitting on a stone, and providing physical support. They are distinct from the collective groups mentioned (Amalek, Israel) and from the divine character (YHWH/God).
